name: Procedural Terrain Feature Generation
definition: A procedural method to generate cliffs and overhangs by approximating their topology as a bicubic Bézier surface, combined with a parabolic function to emulate realistic plateaus. It produces local delta values (additive blending) applied directly to volumetric data.
summary: Procedural Terrain Feature Generation creates cliffs and overhangs using explicit Bézier surfaces and parabolic functions, differing from noise-based methods by focusing on sharp geometric primitives.
